root_cause.summary: IpcNamedPipeServerV1::run used the single configured io_timeout_ms (1000 ms in the engine preview) as a hard deadline for every frame read; a connected client that sent nothing for just over one second had its session torn down.
root_cause.empirical_signature: .local/diagnostics/idle-drop: connect ok, first refresh ok, after_idle_ms=1500 refresh FAILED with connected=False (pre-fix)
root_cause.impact: the control model polls at ~1 Hz, so any load-induced poll delay (GC pause, busy engine loop) randomly degraded long-lived UI sessions; this matches the load-sensitive intermittent failure class reported around Issue #278

fix.change: added read_exact_idle_tolerant for the frame length-prefix read: a wait that expires before any byte of the current read arrives is retried while the server is not stopping; once any byte arrives further stalls stay fatal because partial frame state cannot be resumed safely; payload reads and response writes remain strict fail-closed transfers; accept-phase cycling and stop() cancellation behavior are unchanged

coverage: full control-model sequence on the patched engine
bounded IR WAV prepare and phase-policy ACK smoke on the patched engine
Visual Studio/CMake build incl. modified ipc_pipe.cpp

limitations: User-space Windows verification only; no physical audio, WaveRT, HLK or Microsoft signing evidence.
Control-pipe thread only; RT audio thread rules are untouched.
Writes and payload reads remain fail-closed by design; only inter-frame idle waits became non-fatal.
